did_you_know.text: Did you know? After Josiah’s death, the people of the land made Jehoahaz son of Josiah king in Jerusalem.
Did you know? Jehoahaz was only twenty-three years old when he became king, and he reigned for three months.
Did you know? Pharaoh king of Egypt removed Jehoahaz from the throne and imposed a levy on the land of one hundred talents of silver and one talent of gold.
Did you know? Pharaoh made Eliakim, Jehoahaz’s brother, king and changed his name to Jehoiakim; he took Jehoahaz to Egypt.
Did you know? Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon also took some of the articles from the Temple of the Lord to Babylon and placed them in his temple there.
Did you know? Jehoiachin became king at the age of eight and reigned in Jerusalem for only three months and ten days.
Did you know? Nebuchadnezzar brought Jehoiachin to Babylon along with the precious articles from the Temple of the Lord, and made Zedekiah king in his place.

Did you know? Zedekiah rebelled against the king of Babylon, even though he had sworn an oath of loyalty to him, and he also refused to heed the words of the prophet Jeremiah, spoken at the command of the Lord.

Did you know? According to the chapter, the Lord repeatedly sent his prophets to the people out of compassion for his people and his dwelling place, but the people despised their words and mocked his messengers.

Did you know? In the first year of Cyrus king of Persia, the Lord stirred his spirit, and Cyrus issued a proclamation to build the Temple of the Lord in Jerusalem and invited anyone among his people to go up there.
